statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail 7% (low) with Nasdaq-100 futures inside the CME weekend halt and no live price path available.
recommendation: Tail remains far below the block threshold because no tradable path can form while futures are halted; Stress stays elevated on multi-decade-high Treasury yields and unresolved Strait of Hormuz diplomacy carried into the 22:00 UTC Sunday reopen.
headline: Weekend halt after an orderly Friday close: Tail low, Stress elevated on record-era yields
body: Nasdaq-100 index futures have been halted since Friday 21:00 UTC and do not reopen until 22:00 UTC on Sunday, twelve hours beyond this forecast window, so every hour assessed here sits inside a closed market. Friday's cash session ended constructively and without pathological structure: NDX closed 30,608.14, up 0.42%, inside a 30,413.59-30,667.56 range, off the session high and below the 30,770.63 52-week high, while the S&P 500 added 0.51% and the Dow 0.93%. VIX fell 5.1% to 14.87, near the low of its 14.68-15.94 range. Megacap performance was dispersed rather than one-way, with MSFT up 3.7% and QCOM up 4.0% against META down 3.3% and INTC down 3.5%, which is characteristic of rotation rather than of the persistent directional efficiency that defines Tail. The stressful part of the backdrop is in rates: the 10-year Treasury yield reached 5.225% on Friday, its highest since 2007, and the 30-year touched 5.502%, with the market pricing a further Fed tightening step. Equities absorbed that move rather than breaking on it. WTI settled at $92.41, down 2.3% on the day and 7.4% on the week but still up 12.4% on the month, after Iran offered at the UN to open the Strait of Hormuz within seven days if Washington re-implements the June memorandum. That offer is genuinely two-sided and unresolved across the weekend. Conflicting rate and equity signals of this kind raise Stress and reduce conviction; they do not by themselves establish the mean-reversion failure that Tail measures. The shared Finviz context file was more than three hours old at assessment time and therefore outside its 90-minute freshness window; its megacap section was used only as corroboration after Friday's closing prices were verified against primary sources.

lookbackSummary: Twenty-three of the past twenty-four hourly slots carry a published Claude assessment; the 2026-09-25T13:00Z hour has none and remains explicitly unavailable. The window spans Friday's U.S. session, where Tail sat in the 19-22 range with WATCH mapped at the highs, and the post-settlement weekend halt, where Tail decayed steadily to 8 and Stress eased from the mid-50s to the mid-40s as the session's directional question closed out.
outlookSummary: All twenty-four forecast hours fall inside the CME weekend halt, which runs until 22:00 UTC on Sunday. Tail is held in the 6-8 band throughout because a pathological price path cannot form in a closed market; the small late-window uptick is accumulated gap risk ahead of the reopen rather than any observed structure. Stress stays elevated at 45-48 on multi-decade-high Treasury yields, a hawkish rate path and unresolved Hormuz diplomacy, and the mode turns mixed in the final four hours to reflect genuinely conflicting rate and equity signals. Confidence decays from 82 to 76 as Friday's settlement ages with no live price path to refresh it.
